value.body: A mineral processing engineer works in the plant that turns mined ore into concentrate by crushing, grinding, washing and separating it. Employers include metal and mineral mining companies, coal washeries, iron-ore beneficiation plants and equipment suppliers. A typical day involves shift supervision, checking recovery and grade numbers, and troubleshooting equipment.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech Mining or Mineral Engineering; metallurgy graduates also enter

items.label: Common processes
items.value: Crushing, grinding, flotation, gravity and magnetic separation

items.label: Work location
items.value: Plants at or near mine sites

items.label: Reporting mines
items.note: Excludes petroleum, natural gas, atomic and minor minerals; ~800 metallic and ~1,250 non-metallic

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join as graduate engineer trainees in mining or metal companies through campus hiring, and are posted to plant operations. Shift work at remote sites is standard in the first years.

value.title: At a glance
items: Postings are usually at remote mine sites.
Next roles: plant shift in-charge, process superintendent, plant manager.

competition.note: B.Tech / B.E. (all branches) graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
